metaDescription: Get a Singapore eSIM on StarHub 5G with 1-50 GB plans from $0.30/day. Install by scanning a QR code and keep your own number for calls and texts.
intro: An eSIMFlys eSIM keeps you online in Singapore from the moment you land, without hunting for a local SIM card or a public Wi-Fi signal. It's a digital SIM you install by scanning a QR code, so there's no plastic card to swap. Your plan runs on StarHub 5G, and your regular SIM stays in place for calls and texts.
countryContext: Singapore is a destination in Asia and a popular stop for travelers heading across the region, whether for work, a short stay, or a connecting flight. Data plans here connect through StarHub, a local mobile network. Having a working connection ready before you arrive means you can find directions, check bookings, and message home without delay.
networkNotes: In Singapore, your eSIMFlys data plan connects to StarHub, using its 5G service where available. You don't choose or configure the network by hand — once the eSIM is installed and data roaming is switched on for that line, your phone registers with the local network automatically. No physical SIM swap and no store visit are needed.
connectionDetails: Singapore plans are fixed-data bundles from $0.30/day, in sizes of 1, 3, 5, 10, 20, and 50 GB, with validity of either 7 or 30 days. Choose a smaller tier for maps, messaging, and email, or a larger one for video and heavier browsing. Every plan supports a top-up if you need more data.
activationNotes: Install your eSIM over Wi-Fi before you leave, while you still have a reliable connection. You'll scan a QR code to add the plan, then leave it ready. Most plans begin counting once the eSIM first connects to a network in Singapore, so activation lines up with your arrival. Turn on data roaming for the eSIM line.
whyEsim: An eSIM means you land in Singapore already connected, with no queue at an airport kiosk and no need to switch on your home carrier's roaming. Because it's digital, you set everything up before departure and keep your existing SIM in the phone. If your device is eSIM-capable and carrier-unlocked, you're ready to go.

faqs.q: Which network will my eSIM use in Singapore, and will my phone work?
faqs.a: Your eSIMFlys data runs on StarHub, including its 5G service where available; your phone connects automatically once the eSIM is installed. You'll need an eSIM-capable, carrier-unlocked phone — most iPhone XS and newer, Google Pixel 3 and newer, and Samsung Galaxy S20 and newer qualify. Dial *#06# to check for an EID.

faqs.q: When does my Singapore plan start counting?
faqs.a: Most plans begin when the eSIM first connects to a network in Singapore, not at the moment you buy it. That's why you can install it on Wi-Fi before you fly and keep it ready. Validity then runs for the period you chose — either 7 or 30 days — from that first connection.

faqs.q: Can I keep my usual phone number while I'm there?
faqs.a: Yes. The eSIM is data-only, so it handles your mobile internet while your usual SIM stays active for calls and texts on your existing number. There's no need to remove your physical SIM — the eSIM runs as a separate line that you use for data in Singapore.

faqs.q: How much data should I choose for a trip to Singapore?
faqs.a: It depends on your trip length and habits. The smallest 1 GB tier suits a short visit with light use like maps and messaging, while 5 or 10 GB covers everyday browsing, email, and some video across a week. For longer stays or heavy streaming, the 20 or 50 GB plans give more headroom, and every plan can be topped up if you run low.
